subject.title: Gateway restart failure should keep previous instance running to avoid total disconnect

question: Should OpenClaw make old-instance-preserving gateway handoff a supported restart contract, and on which supervisors should it apply first?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the durable fix crosses process locks, ports, service managers, channel listener duplication, rollback, and user notification semantics that need owner-approved product and architecture direction before implementation.

options.title: Design cross-platform atomic handoff
options.body: Define the health, lock, port, supervisor, and channel-listener contract before implementing the restart behavior across gateway modes.

options.title: Scope to one supervisor first
options.body: Start with the highest-value managed platform and document explicit fallback behavior for supervisors that cannot safely overlap listeners.

options.title: Keep current restart model
options.body: Treat deferral and post-restart health checks as the supported behavior and document that failed restarts may require operator recovery.

recommendation.title: Design cross-platform atomic handoff
recommendation.body: Define the health, lock, port, supervisor, and channel-listener contract before implementing the restart behavior across gateway modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the recent merger/coauthor on the current gateway lifecycle surface and is the better available owner for the product-direction call than the contributor-only issue opener.
